selected_entry_before.title: The deformed tensor space for the type-A finite W-algebra
selected_entry_before.statement: Fix the pyramid $\lambda$, the origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the truncated tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$: as a vector space it is $V^{\otimes d}$, it carries the left action of $U(\mathfrak p)$ twisted by $\eta_c$, $\eta_c(e_{i,j})=e_{i,j}+\delta_{i,j}c_{\mathrm{col}(i)}$, and the right action of the cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$, $\Lambda=\sum_{j}\Lambda_{c_j+q_j-n} on the appropriate integer-coset chains$, defined on the generators by $s_i\mapsto$ place permutation of the $i$-th and $(i+1)$-th factors and $x_1\mapsto (e+\sum_{j=1}^N(c_{\mathrm{col}(j)}+q_{\mathrm{col}(j)}-n)e_{j,j})\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}-\sum_{k=2}^d\sum_{\mathrm{col}(i)<\mathrm{col}(j)}e_{i,j}\otimes1^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes e_{j,i}\otimes1^{\otimes(d-k)}$ and $x_{j+1}\mapsto s_jx_js_j+s_j$; the action is well defined by the cyclotomic-quotient lemma. Restricting the left action from $U(\mathfrak p)$ to $W(\lambda)$ makes $V_c^{\otimes d}$ a filtered $(W(\lambda),H_d(\Lambda))$-bimodule. The associated graded of this bimodule is the Vust tensor space: $\mathrm{gr}\,V_c^{\otimes d}\cong V^{\otimes d}$ with the left $U(\mathfrak g^e)$-action and the right $C_l[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$-action of Vust's theorem, where $\mathrm{gr}\,x_1=e\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}$ and $\mathrm{gr}\,s_i$ is the place permutation. The canonical isomorphism $\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to V_c^{\otimes d}$ of Skryabin's equivalence is an isomorphism of $(W(\lambda),H_d)$-bimodules, and the two actions commute: $W(\lambda)$ and $H_d(\Lambda)$ generate mutual centralizers of the filtered tensor space (proved in the next item).
selected_entry_before.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Restrict the ordinary p tensor action twisted by c to W. The explicit tail/head χ equations from Skryabin's tensor identification give the displayed x_1: the diagonal is c_col+q_col−n, and the negative cross-column correction has the displayed order. Recursion gives the other x_j and matrix-unit expansion gives the affine relations. The raw tensor action commutes with W because its χ equations identify it with the transported universal Casimir action. The cyclotomic supplier proves its exact polynomial, not just its spectrum. With column grading the c and diagonal corrections are lower degree and the cross-column term has degree0; leading x_1=e_1 and leading W=U(g^e). Thus the associated graded tensor action is exactly Vust's. Associativity follows from uniqueness of the Taylor PBW solution. Full details are the finite-W matrix proof §4 and the Casimir suppliers. In this identification the prefix T modes retain their actual displacement index. The loop symbol of T_ij^(r+1) uses the supplier K index r; the finite xi row/box bijection does not alter the physical box labels in x_1.

selected_entry_after.title: The deformed tensor space for the type-A finite W-algebra
selected_entry_after.statement:
Fix the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, its box-labelled natural module $V=\mathbb C^N$,
an arbitrary origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$.
Assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the imported Skryabin and Vust inputs.
For $X\in\mathfrak p$ define the column-trace character
$$\kappa_c(X)=\sum_{b=1}^l c_b\operatorname{tr}(X_{bb}),$$
where $X_{bb}$ is its $b$th column-Levi diagonal block. Write
$\eta_c(X)=X+\kappa_c(X)1$ for the resulting automorphism of $U(\mathfrak p)$,
so $\eta_c(e_{a,b})=e_{a,b}+\delta_{a,b}c_{\operatorname{col}(a)}$.
Let $\mathbb C_c$ be the corresponding one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module
and set $a_b=c_b+q_b-n$ and $\Lambda=\sum_{b=1}^l\Lambda_{a_b}$, with a
separate integer chain for each complex coset as in
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]].

The **truncated (deformed) tensor space** $E_c=V_c^{\otimes d}$ is
$E=V^{\otimes d}$ with the left $U(\mathfrak p)$-action obtained by composing
the ordinary total tensor representation $\rho_d$ with $\eta_c$.
Equivalently it is $\mathbb C_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, with one character
factor; the origin twist is applied once to the total action. For $d\ge1$
its right $H_d(\Lambda)$-action is determined by place permutations $s_i$ and
$$x_1\mapsto\Bigl(e+\sum_{j=1}^N(c_{\operatorname{col}(j)}+q_{\operatorname{col}(j)}-n)e_{j,j}\Bigr)\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}-\sum_{k=2}^d\sum_{\operatorname{col}(i)<\operatorname{col}(j)}e_{i,j}\otimes1^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes e_{j,i}\otimes1^{\otimes(d-k)},$$
with $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$. Here the generator-fixing anti-involution of
the Hecke algebra converts the displayed operators into a right action.
For $d=0$ there are no $x_j,s_i$, $H_0(\Lambda)=\mathbb C$, and $E_c=\mathbb C_c$.

Grade the box basis by $\deg v_a=l-\operatorname{col}(a)$, use the total
tensor grading and its induced endomorphism filtration, and use the fixed
loop chart $\zeta\colon\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)\to U(\mathfrak g^e)$ of
[[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]:
$\zeta(\operatorname{gr}_rT_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$.
The coefficient index remains the actual unshifted $T=FDE$ index of
[[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]].
The restricted character on the fixed centralizer basis is
$$\kappa_c(e_{i,j;r})=\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c),\qquad \sigma_i(c)=\sum_{b=1}^{p_i}c_b.$$
Consequently the **full graded left representation** in this fixed chart is
$$\varphi_{d,c}(X)=\sum_{t=1}^d X^{(t)}+\kappa_c(X)\operatorname{id}_E\qquad(X\in\mathfrak g^e),$$
where $X^{(t)}$ acts in tensor position $t$. In particular its complete
mode-symbol dictionary is
$$\operatorname{gr}_r\Phi_{d,c}(T_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^r\left(\sum_{t=1}^d e_{i,j;r}^{(t)}+\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c)\operatorname{id}_E\right),$$
where $\Phi_{d,c}$ is the restricted $W(\lambda)$-action. On the right,
$\operatorname{gr}_1x_j=e^{(j)}$ and $\operatorname{gr}_0s_i$ is the place
permutation. Thus the graded bimodule is the character-twisted Vust module
$\mathbb C_{\kappa_c|\mathfrak g^e}\otimes E$, with the ordinary truncated
polynomial/permutation action. It need not be the untwisted Vust module in
the fixed chart. Nevertheless its unital left image algebra and its
commutant are exactly the untwisted Vust image algebra and commutant, as
proved below.

The displayed right operators commute with $W(\lambda)$; full
$\mathfrak p$-commutation is not asserted. They make $E_c$ a filtered
$(W(\lambda),H_d(\Lambda))$-bimodule. The actual balanced Skryabin map gives
a coherent isomorphism
$\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to E_c$ of
$(W(\lambda),H_d)$-bimodules. For every complex origin, every pyramid and
every $d$, the two filtered image algebras are mutual centralizers, and their
associated graded image algebras are the unital Vust image algebras. No
admissibility or stable-range restriction enters this centralizer assertion.

If the pyramid is empty, $N=l=0$, use $V=0$ and $W=U(\mathfrak g^e)=\mathbb C$.
For $d=0$ all structures are scalar; for $d>0$, $E=0$ and the empty
cyclotomic product is $1$, giving the zero quotient and zero endomorphism
algebra. All formulas and centralizer identities then have these evident
empty interpretations.
selected_entry_after.strategy: Assume AC for the actual Skryabin and Vust suppliers. The column-trace Lie character $\kappa_c(X)=\sum_b c_b\operatorname{tr}(X_{bb})$ defines the total origin twist once. Use the actual balanced $\mu$ and ambient trace-form Casimir; evaluation on its Whittaker preimages separates nonnegative-column terms, negative character terms, first-position replacements and cross-position replacements, giving exactly the displayed raw $x_1$. Thus affine relations and commutation are transported with $W$, not with all of $\mathfrak p$. First-column filtration gives the full cyclotomic polynomial, and the total tensor grading gives its exact minimal degree, including repeated roots. Restrict the column character to the fixed basis: $\kappa_c(e_{i,j;r})=\delta_{ij}\delta_{r0}\sum_{b\le p_i}c_b$. The graded automorphism $\tau_c(X)=X+\kappa_c(X)1$ preserves $U(\mathfrak g^e)$, and the full fixed-chart graded representation is $\operatorname{gr}\Phi_{d,c}=\varphi_{d,0}\tau_c\zeta$, including its surviving degree-zero scalar. Keep the actual $T=FDE$ coefficient index, $T^{(r+1)}$ loop degree $r$ and sign $(-1)^r$. The right symbols are individual $e$ operators and places. Since $\tau_c$ is a unital automorphism, the exact character-twisted representation has the same unital graded image and commutant as untwisted Vust. Prove the two full filtered centralizer identities by the chains $A^0\subseteq\operatorname{gr}C\subseteq\operatorname{gr}Z(D)\subseteq Z(\operatorname{gr}D)\subseteq Z(D^0)=A^0$ and its reverse counterpart, then finite descending subtraction. Handle $d=0$ with the nontrivial character on the scalar module and the empty pyramid by its zero/scalar identities. Rank-one $c_1=1,d=1$ yields fixed generator $E_{11}=2$, not untwisted $1$; the $\mathfrak{gl}_2$ example gives $[E_{11}-E_{22},x_1]=2E_{12}\ne0$. All origins, shapes and degrees are retained; no stable range or admissibility is used. Mathematical acceptance and actual-supplier/consumer closure remain with the original reviewer.
